Starting next week, we're teaching Lean for Scientists and Engineers!
Twice weekly, 1-3 pm ET, July 9 – August 21, 2024
In person at UMBC and online from anywhere

Lean 4 is a new programming language whose type system enables it to describe and check the logic of advanced math proofs.
By writing software in Lean and writing proofs about those functions, we can have confidence that our code is correct. Our vision is to enable a new class of scientific computing software whose functions are interwoven with a library of formally-verified scientific derivations.

All are welcome! This course is designed for non-mathematicians. Prerequisites: Calculus II; introductory physics and chemistry.
This course is free and not for credit.

Topics:
Logic and proofs for scientists and engineers
Functional programming in Lean 4
Provably-correct programs for scientific computing

Register here: https://forms.gle/Yro7uVoLkxyAyw7r5

Special thanks to @Tomas Skrivan for contributing a lecture on SciLean, as well!

(Once I make the official course link live, I'll add it to the Lean for teaching resources)
